t: Nanomaterial Characterization Data Processor — Overview and definition
description: Analyzes microscopy and spectroscopy data for nanoscale features.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Analyzes microscopy and spectroscopy data for nanoscale features. A nanomaterial data processor quantifies particle-size distributions from TEM, layer counts from AFM/Raman, and composition from EDS/EELS. Real implementations are Python pipelines (HyperSpy, scikit-image) and vendor software. It calibrates scale bars, fits distributions, and reports uncertainties.

body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Nanomaterial Characterization Data Processor, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Particle-size distribution from TEM/SEM). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Particle-size distribution from TEM/SEM and AFM step-height and roughness analysis. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Scanning electron microscopy image analysis tool) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
